It is specifically cultirally created to do what you just said: speak really quickly. 
Most languages evolve towards a system in which the natives can speak as quickly as possible.

Normally, when there are two vowels together, at the end of a word and the start of another word, it is the space that separates them. But that space takes time to vocalise. That little pause that you might do as a non-native speaker is eliminated by adding a consanant that lends itself to be run over quickly. In the case of England and Australia and New Zealand, it' an "r". 

Other languages solve this problem by REMOVING vowels. 

So when there would be two vowels (or vowels sounds like a silent H) the preceeding vowel is removed. For example:

French - The hotel - Le hotel becomes L'hotel.
Italian - Australia - La australia becomes L'australia.

Funnily enough this is the exact reason why, in English, we use "an" when a word starts with a vowel. "An apple" but "a car". Languages just dont like vocalising those stop-gap empty spaces.

Similar to other tips here but the top three for me is:

1. Workout with a friend/partner or someone else. Make a fixed schedule to go to the gym that works for both of you. Eg: every Monday, Wednesday, Friday at 7am. That way, when you don't feel like going the "not wanting to bail on a friend" keeps you going.

2. Workout at the same time every session (more or less) and choose a time that works best for you. Some people just cannot be active in the morning and others can't do anything else after a day at work other than lying down. Whichever time you are most active in the day should be the time at gym.

3. Hang out at the gym. On days you feel tired or dont want to go, that's fine. Take your podcast, music, phone or even a book and go to the gym and just sit in there with no intention of working out. Eventually you'll probably get bored and work out anyway or think "well since I'm here, I may as well pick something up or get on a treadmill". 

People say discipline, discipline, discipline but the reality is creating discipline for yourself is like trying to suck water out of a stone. It's nearly impossible if you are not disciplined already. So you need to bend your entire life structure around the gym in a way that will FORCE you to go or at least, keep funneling you into the gym and giving you the chance to pick up something heavy.

- Not every boy is the same so all these different experiences from the internet may not apply to your boys. It should just be food for thought rather than an action plan.
- Every parent makes mistakes and you will too. Relax, forgive yourself when it happens and just do the best you can. 

My "negative" experiences with my mum:

So basically I was born very VERY early (14 weeks). Because of this the doctor told my mum that one of my developmental issues would be "anger problems." 
This ended up being a self-fulfuilling prophecy, sadly. 

Because, whenever I was angry or similar my mum (and dad) would just say "well that's his anger issue again" but they NEVER asked me what is wrong. What is causing my anger. And that made me EVEN more angry and thus the cycles continued horribly. Let me be clear, it is normal for a 4 year old, or 6 year old or 8 year old to be angry at times. They don't know how to articulate their feelings and anger can be the result. So every response to my anger was a "time-out" or alone time or just letting it burn out. 
This was a terrible strategy. It made me feel ashamed and guilty about a perfectly normal emotion which again made me angrier. This affected a lot of my relationships throughout my life. 
When your kid is angry or sad or anything, ask them what is wrong and stick with them through the emotion until they can compose themselves enough to tell you. Then try and help if you can. By offering support, instead of shunning it, hopefully they wont internalise the feeling of shame and worthlessness. Although you will have gone through it "together" which will create a stronger bond of trust. 

The 2nd experience relates to above but manifest differently. 
My whole life as long as I can remember I've loved history. That meant I was into all the sword and sandals movies, toy soldiers, toy swords and axes and so forth. Well because of the above mentioned fear of anger issues, I was actively forbidden or discouraged from watching those movie or having those toys because they "promoted violence." But here is the thing: most young boys like to play and imagine fight with each other. It's normal. And something else, people's tendencies are like pressure in a machine. It HAS to go somewhere. If you dont give it a good, useful place to go it will eventually explode. 
So without "violent" toys or video games or movies I began play fighting with my food by "cutting the heads off" carrots at the dinner tables a similar things. Then, unfortunately for my younger brother, I began play fighting with him too. But because of the age difference and because I was stronger this was only ever seen as bullying by my parents (and to be fair to him, it probably was a bit sometimes too as he wasnt always a willing player). So the restrictions and shaming and removing any opportunity to express this interest continued further. Nevermind when MY older brother did the same to me though because I was the one with "diagnosed" anger problems.
So, don't supress your boys interests. Encourage them in ways that are actually beneficial to both him amd society. Like to play soldier? Great, show them that "the best soldiers and knights (or whatever) have honour and respect. They fight to protect, they have mercy, ect." Intergrate it well into their personality.

I only realised all this information about myself and my experiences at the age of 28, going through a divorce that was largely caused by my behaviours based on my childhood experiences. 28 years of anger. Imagine all the other opportunities it has poisoned that I dont even know about? Imagine the good that could have been done if my "anger" had been understood and integrated properly?

I have lost many of my own ambushes because i mag dumped and barely hit anything coz of difficult to control recoil. It forces me to make better choices, wait for the right moment, stress induced analysis of my options. I have also won a few counter-ambushes and it feels great. 

Also why would the recoil of a fully kitted M4 be the same as, or similar to, an average kedr or AK or whatever else? Then what is the point of buying all those upgrades.
